%20%20%20Pause%20before%20the%20practice%20problems%20and%20answer%20these%20without%20looking%20back%20at%20the%20code.%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20In%20a%20series%20arrangement%2C%20which%20quantity%20is%20shared%20by%20the%20elements%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20In%20a%20parallel%20arrangement%2C%20which%20quantity%20is%20shared%20by%20the%20elements%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20Why%20does%20a%20Maxwell%20model%20creep%20indefinitely%20under%20constant%20load%3F%0A%20%20%20%204.%20Why%20does%20a%20Voight%20model%20lack%20an%20instantaneous%20finite%20deformation%20under%20constant%20load%3F%0A%20%20%20%205.%20Why%20can%20the%20Kelvin%20solid%20model%20both%20jump%20immediately%20and%20still%20creep%20toward%20an%20asymptote%3F%0A%20%20%20%206.%20In%20a%20muscle-tendon%20model%2C%20where%20would%20you%20place%20the%20active%20force%20generator%20relative%20to%20passive%20elastic%20and%20viscous%20elements%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.accordion(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%7B'Checkpoint%20answers'%3A%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Force.%202.%20Deformation.%203.%20The%20dashpot%20keeps%20flowing%20under%20constant%20force.%204.%20The%20parallel%20dashpot%20prevents%20an%20instantaneous%20length%20jump%20under%20finite%20force.%205.%20The%20series%20spring%20supplies%20the%20immediate%20extension%20and%20the%20Voigt%20branch%20supplies%20bounded%20creep.%206.%20The%20active%20contractile%20element%20is%20typically%20parallel%20to%20passive%20fiber%20elasticity%20and%20in%20series%20with%20tendon%20elasticity%3B%20passive%20damping%20is%20an%20additional%20modeling%20choice.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%7D%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20expanded%3DFalse%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Problems%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Work%20through%20these%20after%20reading%20the%20chapter.%20Use%20the%20code%20above%20as%20a%20starting%20point%2C%20but%20first%20write%20the%20equations%20on%20paper.%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20**Parameter%20audit.**%20For%20the%20Maxwell%20constant-deformation%20response%2C%20double%20%5C(b%5C)%20and%20then%20double%20%5C(k%5C).%20Which%20change%20increases%20the%20relaxation%20time%20constant%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%202.%20**Creep%20comparison.**%20Choose%20%5C(k%5C)%20and%20%5C(b%5C)%20values%20so%20the%20Voight%20model%20reaches%20approximately%2095%20percent%20of%20its%20final%20deformation%20by%20%5C(t%3D3%5C)%20s%20under%20a%20constant%20load.%0A%0A%20%20%20%203.%20**Kelvin%20design.**%20Choose%20%5C(k_s%5C)%2C%20%5C(k_p%5C)%2C%20and%20%5C(b%5C)%20so%20the%20Kelvin%20solid%20has%20a%20large%20immediate%20deformation%20but%20only%20a%20small%20additional%20creep.%0A%0A%20%20%20%204.%20**Force%20relaxation.**%20For%20the%20Kelvin%20solid%2C%20calculate%20%5C(F_0%5C)%20and%20%5C(F_%5Cinfty%5C)%20by%20hand%20for%20the%20parameters%20used%20in%20this%20notebook.%20Check%20your%20calculation%20against%20the%20plot.%0A%0A%20%20%20%205.%20**Sinusoidal%20input.**%20In%20the%20prescribed-deformation%20simulation%2C%20increase%20the%20frequency%20and%20describe%20how%20peak%20force%20changes%20in%20each%20model.%0A%0A%20%20%20%206.%20**Muscle-model%20bridge.**%20Sketch%20a%20simple%20Hill-type%20muscle%20model%20and%20label%20which%20parts%20are%20passive%20elastic%2C%20passive%20viscous%2C%20and%20active%20force-generating%20elements.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.accordion(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%7B'Final%20answers%20to%20original%20Problems'%3A%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Doubling%20%24b%24%20doubles%20relaxation%20time%3B%20doubling%20%24k%24%20halves%20it.%0A%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Any%20%24b%2Fk%3D3%2F%5B-%5Cln(0.05)%5D%5Capprox1.00142%24%20s%20reaches%20exactly%2095%25%20at%203%20s%3B%20%24b%2Fk%3D1%24%20s%20gives%20about%2095.02%25.%0A%0A%20%20%20%203.%20One%20example%20is%20%24k_s%3D20%24%2C%20%24k_p%3D200%24%20N%2Fm%2C%20%24b%3D40%24%20N%20s%2Fm%3A%20additional%20creep%20is%2010%25%20of%20the%20immediate%20deformation.%0A%0A%20%20%20%204.%20%24F_0%3Dk_sx_0%24%20and%20%24F_%5Cinfty%3Dk_sk_px_0%2F(k_s%2Bk_p)%24.%20For%20the%20default%20%24k_s%3D120%24%2C%20%24k_p%3D80%24%20N%2Fm%2C%20these%20are%20%24120x_0%24%20and%20%2448x_0%24%20N%2C%20with%20%24x_0%24%20in%20metres.%0A%0A%20%20%20%205.%20At%20fixed%20sinusoidal%20displacement%20amplitude%2C%20Voigt%20force%20amplitude%20grows%20without%20bound%20with%20frequency%3B%20Maxwell%20approaches%20stiffness%20%24k%24%20and%20the%20series-spring%2FVoigt%20Kelvin%20model%20approaches%20stiffness%20%24k_s%24.%20Transient%20and%20offset%20forces%20can%20also%20affect%20the%20plotted%20maximum.%0A%0A%20%20%20%206.%20The%20active%20contractile%20element%20acts%20alongside%20a%20passive%20parallel%20elastic%20element%20and%20in%20series%20with%20the%20tendon%20elastic%20element%3B%20a%20passive%20dashpot%20may%20represent%20additional%20viscous%20losses.%20A%20Hill%20force%E2%80%93velocity%20curve%20is%20not%20itself%20an%20ordinary%20passive%20dashpot.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%7D%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20expanded%3DFalse%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Go%20deeper%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Use%20%5BKineticsFundamentalConcepts%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fkinetics_fundamental_concepts.py)%20to%20connect%20this%20guide%20with%20the%20surrounding%20mechanics%20and%20modeling%20material.%20Return%20to%20the%20assumptions%20behind%20each%20equation%20when%20applying%20it%20to%20a%20new%20experiment.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Video%20lectures%20on%20the%20Internet%0A%0A%20%2
